Thanks for the ping — quick commercial proposal below that I think is a reasonable middle ground. Attaching a short workbook with numbers.

Proposed commercial slate (high level):
- Minimum commit: move to an annual commitment of $500k but allow quarterly proration and rebalancing: customer is billed 25% of the annual commit each quarter; if actual usage in a quarter < billed commit, we credit the following quarter up to one quarter; if usage is above billed commit, standard overage rates apply.
- Overage: 1.2x the blended committed rate per token for overages beyond quarterly billed amount (this preserves predictability).
- Price tiers: keep the draft breakpoints but add explicit per-token rates for each tier and a clear example calculation in the OF.
- Invoice cadence: monthly in arrears referencing quarterly billed commit; invoices must include PO number.
- Net terms: we can accept Net45, but propose a 1.5% early payment discount if paid within 15 days.
- Taxes: we propose Redwood invoices exclusive of taxes; customer is responsible for VAT/GST. Redwood will include tax as a separate line if we are required to collect.

I think this preserves Redwood unit economics while accommodating Zephyr's AP rhythm. If finance/legal are good with the wording, we can send a consolidated redline back to Elena with these points.

Attachment: Proposed_Commercials.xlsx

—Ben

Ben — good commercial approach. A few legal redlines and comments to protect Redwood and keep contract clean:

1) Taxes: proposed language — "Customer shall be responsible for all sales, use, value-added, and similar taxes arising from Redwood's provision of services under this Order Form, excluding taxes based on Redwood's net income. Redwood will list applicable taxes as separate line items on invoices. If Customer is required by law to withhold taxes, Customer shall provide evidence and Redwood will invoice gross-up only where required by law." Avoid broad gross-up language; don't accept customer indemnifying Redwood for taxes unless narrow.

2) Proration/credits: accept quarterly billing with one-quarter carry-forward credit for under-utilization. However, do not allow credits to be banked beyond the following quarter. Add explicit example in the OF to avoid later disputes.

3) PO requirement: invoices will reference Customer PO when provided. Do not condition the effectiveness of the Order Form on issuance of a PO. If Zephyr requires PO binding language, limit it to invoice processing only.

4) Net terms & late fees: Net45 acceptable. Add standard late fee interest (1.5% per month) and require that any disputed amounts are raised within 45 days of invoice date.

5) Audit/rights: retain MSA audit language but narrow to one audit per 12 months and only for reconciliation of committed volumes; Redwood to be given 30 days notice.

I'll attach a marked-up draft of the OF and a short email paragraph you can send to the customer.

Attachment: Legal_Redline_2.0.docx

—Laura

Elena / Mike — thanks for the redlines and patience. We've reviewed internally and are attaching a consolidated set of redlines that incorporate commercial, legal, and finance positions (attached). Summary of our proposed positions: 

- Minimum commit/proration: Agree to annual $500k commitment with quarterly proration (25% billed per quarter). Under-utilization credits can be carried forward into the following quarter only; credits expire after that. Detailed example is included on page 2 of the attached.
- Overage rate: 1.2x blended committed rate for usage beyond the quarterly billed amount. We added a worked example for clarity.
- Invoice cadence & PO: Invoices will be issued monthly in arrears and will reference the Customer PO when provided. We cannot make the Order Form effectiveness conditional on the PO issuance.
- Net terms: We can accept Net45 as requested. Redwood will include a 1.5% discount for payments received within 15 days (early payment discount). Late payments will accrue interest at 1.5% per month.
- Taxes: Customer is responsible for VAT/GST and other transaction taxes; Redwood will invoice exclusive of taxes and list taxes as separate line items when applicable. If law requires Redwood to collect tax, it will appear on the invoice.
